hypothesis: For registered finite deterministic agents, future-commitment equivalence is invariant to destructive coordinate recoding but changes under a delayed load-bearing transition mutation that preserves coordinates and depth-one commitment observations.

controls.description: Coordinates and transition constraints are both preserved.
Coordinates and geometry are destroyed while transition and commitment structure are preserved exactly by conjugacy.
Coordinates and every depth-one commitment response are preserved while one delayed load-bearing transition changes.
The same coordinate scramble is crossed with the altered transition constraint to complete the factorial.
The paper must preserve the earlier Constraint-Swap rejection and cannot use this exact quotient construction to rescue the failed hidden-geometry mechanism.

gates.criterion: The frozen design, digest, seed sets, family cells, scramble integrity, and 768-row confirmatory schedule are exact.
Exhaustive quotient and product-search checks match T1 through T4 for every registered pair.
Every coordinate-destroyed conjugate preserves the exact quotient and all registered future commitments.
Every coordinate-preserved delayed mutant preserves depth-one commitments but changes the exact quotient with a witness of depth at least two.
Quotient agreement reaches leave-one-family-out balanced accuracy 1.0 while coordinate, current-output, and depth-one baselines are at most 0.5.
The non-necessity, non-sufficiency, and predictor gates pass separately in parity, modulo-three, and order families.
The paper treats the theorem as an automata/bisimulation specialization, preserves the prior geometry null, and withholds learned, stochastic, real-network, and universal claims.
